name: The Cooper Companies, Inc.
sector: Healthcare / Medical devices (contact lenses, women's health & fertility)
moat_justification: Real but moderate franchise: prescription lock-in, premium differentiated lenses (MyDay, MiSight) and a decade of ~66% gross margins, capped at 5 because the ROIC proxy has run only ~3.8-5.1% for six years (FY20-25) — the goodwill-heavy balance sheet has not earned its cost of capital — and share is contested in a four-player oligopoly.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 12 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
BASE_DIVERGENCE: latest FY OE/share 1.82 vs 3-yr median 1.06 — one of them is distorted; find out which and why
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 3.8x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier D (6.9%) vs bull-case tier C (10.1%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: Solid med-device franchise, moat 5/10, but priced for a recovery the model can't see: weighted IRR 8.2% and IV@15% $25.98 vs $57.38 price — clears 15% only below ~$26.
moat_for: CooperVision is a global top-tier contact lens maker with prescription/fitter lock-in — wearers rarely switch brands once fitted
MyDay daily silicone hydrogel and MiSight (only FDA-approved myopia-control lens) are differentiated, premium-priced franchises
Gross margin stable at ~65-67% for a decade, through COVID and the FY26 destocking
CooperSurgical fertility (genomics, lab platforms) holds a strong niche position with recurring services demand
moat_against: ROIC proxy only ~4-5% for six straight years (FY20-25) — the acquisition-heavy balance sheet earns below its cost of capital
Contact lenses are a four-player oligopoly (J&J Vision, Alcon, Bausch + Lomb) — share is contested, not locked
Legacy hydrogel portfolio shrinking double digits; growth depends on MyDay/MiSight mix shift
Paragard faces a new non-hormonal IUD competitor; fertility carries litigation overhang (embryo-culture-media recall settlement)
